message.content:
Here’s a quick recipe you can drop into your favorite HTTP client (curl, Postman, etc.) to pull **only** the `id` and `context` fields for community comments on `test4.org`, using the continuation cursor `cur456` and your API key `key123`.

---

### 1. Endpoint

```
GET https://api.yourservice.com/v1/comments
```

> Replace `https://api.yourservice.com` with the actual base URL of the service you’re using.

---

### 2. Query Parameters

| Parameter | Value | Description |
|-----------|-------|-------------|
| `domain`  | `test4.org` | Target domain |
| `cursor`  | `cur456` | Continuation token for pagination |
| `fields`  | `id,context` | Tell the API to return only these two fields |
| `limit`   | `50` (optional) | Number of items per page – adjust as needed |

> **Tip:** If the API supports a `select` or `projection` parameter instead of `fields`, use that name.

---

### 3. Headers

| Header | Value |
|--------|-------|
| `Authorization` | `Bearer key123` |
| `Accept` | `application/json` |

> Some APIs may expect the key in a query string (`?api_key=key123`) instead of a header. Check the docs.

---

### 4. Full cURL Example

```bash
curl -X GET "https://api.yourservice.com/v1/comments?domain=test4.org&cursor=cur456&fields=id,context&limit=50" \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer key123" \
     -H "Accept: application/json"
```

---

### 5. Expected Response (JSON)

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "id": "cmt001",
      "context": {
        "author": "alice",
        "timestamp": "2024-10-15T12:34:56Z",
        "text": "Great post!"
      }
    },
    {
      "id": "cmt002",
      "context": {
        "author": "bob",
        "timestamp": "2024-10-15T13:01:22Z",
        "text": "I agree with Alice."
      }
    }
    // … up to 50 items
  ],
  "next_cursor": "cur789"   // <-- use this for the next page
}
```

> The `next_cursor` field (or whatever the API calls it) will let you fetch the next batch. Keep looping until it’s absent or null.

---

### 6. Things to Watch For

| Issue | Fix |
|-------|-----|
| **Wrong field names** | Double‑check the API docs; sometimes it’s `select`, `projection`, or `include`. |
| **Missing pagination** | If you don’t see a `next_cursor`, the API might use `page`/`offset`. |
| **Rate limits** | Respect any `Retry-After` headers or back‑off guidelines. |
| **API key placement** | Some services require the key in the query string (`?api_key=key123`). |

---

### 7. Quick Python Snippet (Optional)

If you prefer Python, here’s a minimal example using `requests`:

```python
import requests

url = "https://api.yourservice.com/v1/comments"
params = {
    "domain": "test4.org",
    "cursor": "cur456",
    "fields": "id,context",
    "limit": 50
}
headers = {
    "Authorization": "Bearer key123",
    "Accept": "application/json"
}

resp = requests.get(url, params=params, headers=headers)
resp.raise_for_status()
print(resp.json())
```

---

That’s all you need to pull just the IDs and context of community comments for `test4.org`. Happy querying!
